name: pip
purpose: Python package installer for downloading, inspecting, and managing third-party Python libraries.
explanation: Installs Python libraries from PyPI into your environment's `site-packages` directory and resolves their dependencies automatically.

parameters.description: Downloads and installs `<pkg>` and its dependencies.
Prints version, dependencies, and the exact `Location:` path on disk.
Lists all installed Python packages in the active environment.

example: pip install qrcode && pip show qrcode
expectedOutput:
Name: qrcode
Version: 8.0
Location: /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/.../site-packages
Requires: colorama, pillow
whenToUse: When adding third-party Python libraries such as `Pillow`, `qrcode`, or `pyfiglet` (Worksheet 13b).
commonMistakes: Installing into system Python instead of an active virtual environment, or confusing CLI tools (`brew`/`apt`) with Python libraries (`pip`).
moduleTitle: C13 — Meeting New Tools, Libraries & AI Rules
platformCompatibility: macOS, GNU/Linux, Windows (often `pip3` when multiple Python versions exist)
explanationOfOutput: Displays installed metadata including dependencies and exact filesystem location.

relevantConcepts.title: C13 — Python Libraries & 3 Rules for AI

commonErrors: `ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement ...` (typo in package name)
